extracted text: The Al-Cu 206 cast alloys with varying alloy compositions (i.e., different levels of Fe, Mn, and Si) were investigated to evaluate the effect of the iron-rich intermetallics on the tensile properties. In each test, approximately 30 kg of material was melted, and a master alloy of Al-5 pct Ti-1 pct B was added to obtain approximately 0.2 pct Ti for grain refinement. The alloys usually have a severe stress cracking corrosion tendency in the T6 condition (solution treatment and artificial peak aging); thus, the most frequently used tempers are T4 and T7, which were employed in this study. T4 refers to solution and natural aging condition, while T7 refers to solution and artificial overaging condition. The experimental designation XXX indicates the first digit stands for the approximate content of Fe (B for baseline at a maximum specification limit of 0.15 pct Fe), and the second and third digits stand for Si and Mn contents, respectively.
property mapping:
- AA: The alloys are described as "Al-Cu 206 cast alloys" in the abstract and introduction
- temper: T4 (solution and natural aging) and T7 (solution and artificial overaging)
- YS [MPa]: Yield strength at 0.2% offset strain in Table III
- UTS [MPa]: Ultimate tensile strength in Table III
- elong [%]: Elongation (El) in percentage in Table III
- Fe, Cu, Mg, Si, Mn, Ti: Weight percentages in Table I
abbreviations:
- T4: Solution treatment and natural aging
- T7: Solution treatment and artificial overaging
- UTS: Ultimate Tensile Strength
- YS: Yield Strength at 0.2% offset strain
- El: Elongation
- QI: Quality Index
- β-Fe: Platelet Al7Cu2Fe/Al7Cu2(FeMn) intermetallic phase
- α-Fe: Chinese script Al15(FeMn)3(SiCu)2 intermetallic phase
- Al_m(FeMn): Chinese script aluminum-iron-manganese intermetallic phase
- In the alloy designation (XXX), the first digit stands for the approximate content of Fe (B for baseline at 0.15% Fe max), the second and third digits stand for Si and Mn contents, respectively
weight percentage: The weight percentages for each element are already provided in Table I. All values are in weight percentage (wt%). The aluminum (Al) content is listed as 'bal' which means balance or remainder, i.e., the percentage of Al is 100% minus the sum of all other elements.
